nate: Quick RFC follow-up — after yesterday's perf run I have questions about when we should pick GQA kernels vs MQA kernels in runtime selector. TL;DR numbers below.

jessica: thanks for running it. can you paste the runs?

nate: paste from perf run: 
```
Model: redwood-7b
Batch=1, seq=1024: MQA latency 1.9ms/token, GQA 2.1ms/token, mem(MQA)=7.2GB, mem(GQA)=6.1GB
Batch=8, seq=1024: MQA latency 1.5ms/token, GQA 1.2ms/token, mem(MQA)=10.5GB, mem(GQA)=9.0GB
Batch=1, seq=4096: MQA OOM on rtx-a5000, GQA 3.9ms/token, mem=18GB
```

olga: interesting — MQA wins at low batch & short seq, GQA wins at higher batch or long seq. matches intuition.

mike: do we have numbers on token quality/regression? any correctness difference between MQA & GQA?

nate: no quality diffs for autoregressive gen in these runs (same logits within float noise). main tradeoffs are memory (KV cache layout) and kernel tiling efficiency.

jessica: so selector heuristics we discussed in RFC: check (1) num_heads vs head_dim, (2) seq_len, (3) batch. propose a simple rule: if seq_len >= 2048 -> prefer GQA; else if batch >= 4 and model_heads >= 32 -> prefer GQA; else prefer MQA. thoughts?

olga: sounds OK but add a hard OOM-detection fallback: try MQA fast path, if alloc fails or mem > threshold, fall back to GQA automatically. avoids user perf cliffs.

mike: +1. also, expose an override in model config so model owners can force one kernel (eg: `force_attention=\"mqa\"`).

nate: agreed. putting pseudo-code for selector so it's explicit: 
```
function pick_attention_kernel(model, batch, seq):
  if model.config.force_attention: return model.config.force_attention
  if seq >= 2048: return 'gqa'
  if batch >= 4 and model.num_heads >= 32: return 'gqa'
  if try_allocate_kv_cache(batch, seq, model) == OOM: return 'gqa'
  return 'mqa'
```

jessica: small nit — try_allocate_kv_cache is expensive on hot path. prefer a cheap estimate using formula: kv_bytes = batch * seq * head_dim * 2 (float16) * num_kv_layers. use estimate for decision, only actually catch OOM as safety.

olga: agree. runtime should maintain a tiny per-device cache of last-estimated free bytes to avoid syscalls.

mike: ops impact: changing default selector will change p99 tail for some tenants. we should rollout as canary flag under runtime.v0.9.3 and surface telemetry: selected_kernel, estimate_bytes, actual_alloc, fallback_count.

nate: noted. I'll add telemetry fields and a canary flag. also plan: add a small benchmark harness that runs both kernels on a sample of models nightly to update heuristics.

jessica: action items: (1) nate to add selector + config override + telemetry PR, (2) olga to add cheap estimator util, (3) mike to wire canary and dashboards. mark owners?

nate: I'll open the PR today and link it here. no blockers.

runtime-bot: Deploy check: runtime.v0.9.3-canary flagged in prod cluster alpha-1 (meta)

mike: once PR is up, I'll add the canary flag and create dashboards for selected_kernel distribution and fallback_count.

nate: thanks — will follow up with PR link and perf logs for 13b / 70b too.

jessica: :thumbsup: good follow-up, keep it incremental.
